topicName: Cloud Deployment Manager: Infrastructure as Code
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud Deployment Manager: Infrastructure as Code on Google Cloud"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Deployment Manager (CDM) is Google Cloud's Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service. It allows you to define and manage your Google Cloud resources using declarative configuration files. This tutorial will guide you through the basics of using CDM to provision and manage infrastructure."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Google Cloud project with billing enabled."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The Google Cloud SDK (gcloud) installed and configured."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of YAML or Python."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Deployment Manager Concepts"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into the practical aspects, let's understand the core concepts:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deployment: A collection of Google Cloud resources that are managed as a single unit."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configuration: A YAML or Python file that defines the resources to be created or updated in a deployment."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Template: A reusable configuration file that can be parameterized to create multiple deployments with different configurations."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Schema: Defines the structure and validation rules for your templates."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Simple Deployment"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's create a simple deployment that provisions a single Compute Engine instance. We'll use a YAML configuration file."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a file named 'vm.yaml' with the following content:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"resources:
- name: my-vm
  type: compute.v1.instance
  properties:
    zone: us-central1-a
    machineType: zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-1
    disks:
    - deviceName: boot
      type: PERSISTENT
      boot: true
      autoDelete: true
      initializeParams:
        sourceImage: projects/debian-cloud/global/images/family/debian-10"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"This configuration defines a Compute Engine instance named 'my-vm' in the 'us-central1-a' zone, using the 'n1-standard-1' machine type and a Debian 10 image."},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, deploy this configuration using the gcloud command:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"gcloud deployment-manager deployments create my-first-deployment --config vm.yaml"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates a deployment named 'my-first-deployment' using the 'vm.yaml' configuration file."},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can check the status of the deployment in the Google Cloud Console or using the gcloud command:"},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"gcloud deployment-manager deployments describe my-first-deployment"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Updating a Deployment"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"To update a deployment, modify the configuration file and run the 'update' command:"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, let's change the machine type to 'n1-standard-2' in 'vm.yaml':"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"resources:
- name: my-vm
  type: compute.v1.instance
  properties:
    zone: us-central1-a
    machineType: zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-2
    disks:
    - deviceName: boot
      type: PERSISTENT
      boot: true
      autoDelete: true
      initializeParams:
        sourceImage: projects/debian-cloud/global/images/family/debian-10"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Then, update the deployment:"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"gcloud deployment-manager deployments update my-first-deployment --config vm.yaml"},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Deleting a Deployment"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"To delete a deployment and all its associated resources, use the 'delete' command:"},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"gcloud deployment-manager deployments delete my-first-deployment"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"This will prompt you for confirmation before deleting the deployment. Be careful, as this action is irreversible."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Templates"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Templates allow you to reuse configurations and parameterize them. Let's create a simple template for creating Compute Engine instances."},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a file named 'vm_template.jinja' with the following content:"},{"order":36,"type":"code","text":"{% set zone = properties['zone'] %}
{% set machine_type = properties['machine_type'] %}

resources:
- name: my-vm
  type: compute.v1.instance
  properties:
    zone: '{{ zone }}'
    machineType: '{{ zone }}/machineTypes/{{ machine_type }}'
    disks:
    - deviceName: boot
      type: PERSISTENT
      boot: true
      autoDelete: true
      initializeParams:
        sourceImage: projects/debian-cloud/global/images/family/debian-10"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"This template uses Jinja2 syntax to define parameters for the zone and machine type."},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, create a configuration file named 'vm_config.yaml' that uses this template:"},{"order":39,"type":"code","text":"imports:
- path: vm_template.jinja

resources:
- name: my-vm-instance
  type: vm_template.jinja
  properties:
    zone: us-central1-a
    machine_type: n1-standard-1"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"This configuration imports the 'vm_template.jinja' template and defines the values for the 'zone' and 'machine_type' parameters."},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deploy this configuration using the gcloud command:"},{"order":42,"type":"code","text":"gcloud deployment-manager deployments create my-template-deployment --config vm_config.yaml"},{"order":43,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":44,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Deployment Manager provides a powerful way to manage your Google Cloud infrastructure as code. By using configurations and templates, you can automate the provisioning and management of your resources, ensuring consistency and repeatability. This tutorial covered the basics of creating, updating, and deleting deployments, as well as using templates to create reusable configurations. Explore the official Google Cloud documentation for more advanced features and options."}]
